ai.description: This 10 cm gecko is translucent pinkish-grey with fine dark speckling. It features broad, undivided toe pads and skin that tears easily when handled. It is a member of the family Gekkonidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gehyra mutilata* is best identified by its unique, undivided terminal digital pads and the absence of webbing between its toes, unlike other similar Indian geckos.
ai.habitat: *Gehyra mutilata* inhabits tropical moist forests and human settlements in the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The stump-toed gecko is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy where it can voluntarily shed patches of skin to escape a predator's grasp.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gehyra mutilata* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with females often depositing eggs in communal sites.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gehyra mutilata* is found across the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the Western Ghats and Northeast India, ranging from sea level to approximately 1,500 meters.
